title: New in TravStats {{version}}
subtitle: A short overview of the most important changes.

design.title: One look for web and app
design.body: TravStats now looks like the Companion app: the same colours, spacing and type, one heading per page, a dark mode that comes from the colour tokens instead of special rules. Settings are split into groups: flights, cruises and lodging each have an address of their own, while account, display, data and services are sections on the general page. The admin area is a page of its own beside them — no longer a submenu.

evidence.title: Every number shows what it is made of – and every failure why
evidence.body: Click a figure or a row in a ranking and a panel lists the entries that produced it — flights, cruises, stays, places — with each entry's share. What cannot be attributed is said rather than dropped: a total without an exchange rate stays empty and names the reason. The panel can be shared as a link. The running year compares with the same span of the previous year rather than a whole one — September no longer reads like a collapse. A cruise leg is now measured along the sea route the map draws; until now some legs counted only as a straight line. Your cruise kilometres in the statistics mostly go up as a result, and stored legs are recomputed once on the first start after the update. And when something does not work – a service does not answer, a quota is used up, a backup fails – TravStats now says why instead of quietly carrying on as if nothing happened. A backup taken on an older version can now be restored: TravStats brings it up to date by itself afterwards and says so when that fails.

documents.title: Documents, receipts and costs have a place
documents.body: Boarding passes, hotel invoices and booking confirmations now live as documents on the entry they belong to, and a receipt is attached to what it proves. TravStats reads every document it knows — a photographed invoice, a boarding pass through its barcode, a Booking.com mail through a fixed template — and files it instead of leaving it lying around. When a PDF or an email hangs on a flight, a cruise or a stay, you can take price, currency and booking reference from it — you see every value first and decide what is taken. Costs that belong to no booking – tolls, ferries, parking, fuel – go on the trip or on a roadtrip section; they count in the cost statistics, and deleting a section does not lose its costs, they move to the trip.

entrySuggestions.title: TravStats helps while you enter: suggestions, trip suggestions, loyalty programmes
entrySuggestions.body: Forms suggest what you have entered before: seat, flight number, terminal and frequent-flyer number from your flights, room and board from earlier stays, your tags as a choice while you type, and your recently used currencies first. A new entry lands in the trip whose dates it falls in on its own; cruise stops and stays take their dates from the start and the trip. A suggestion never overwrites what you typed yourself. A new cruise now needs a departure date and something to recognise it by – ship, route name, cruise line or departure port – instead of being saved as an empty row. Hotel chains you create are now yours alone: other accounts on the same instance do not see them. Every loyalty programme – frequent-flyer, hotel and cruise-line programmes – is now managed in one place under Settings → Loyalty programmes: programme, membership number and your current status. On a frequent-flyer programme, one button per alliance – Star Alliance, SkyTeam, oneworld – adds all its airlines at once. A hotel chain's page shows your programme with a badge for the status, and each programme lists its stays and nights or flights per year – every figure leads to the list of hotels or flights behind it. The inbox sorts flight updates, open questions and suggestions into tabs with status counts, and the logbook pages. New is the “Trip suggestions” tab: TravStats reads from flights, cruises, stays and place visits when you were away, and proposes a new trip – or the trip the entries belong to. You accept, edit or dismiss – nothing is created until you accept. The Excel spreadsheet works both ways: edit it and read it back, or carry it into another account. And TravStats can be installed as a web app. The demo account is now an invented traveller from the Rhineland with ten years of travel. A new installation creates it on its own and turns the beta switch on as it does; whoever signs in to the demo account is told so right at the start.

placesPassport.title: Places, the passport and photos
placesPassport.body: Places are a full domain with lists, checklists and a CSV import that also takes a Google Takeout export; the passport shows countries with their evidence. Photos now hang on places too: a gallery with a cover picture, suggestions from your trip photos taken the same day close by, and pictures in the trip journal. Stays, flights and cruises show the trip photos from their own time span, and an accepted photo journey brings its pictures along.

summaryOpenData.title: The AI summary, the AI switch, Dawarich and open data services
summaryOpenData.body: The AI summary of a trip now names only what the data holds, and location history from Dawarich counts as evidence for a country. New, for an admin to switch on: open data services — the weather in the trip journal from Open-Meteo and descriptions from Wikipedia on places and stays. They stay off until someone switches them on, because places and dates of your trips go to those services. The other way round, an admin can switch the AI parser off entirely: TravStats then reads bookings with its built-in templates only, no text goes to a language model, not even a trip summary – and an import says that this is a setting, not a server that is down. Besides Ollama, an OpenAI-compatible AI provider (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama Cloud or your own server) can now read the bookings no template knows — a provider outside your network only once an admin explicitly agrees, and the import tells you which model read it.

app.title: The Companion app
app.body: You pair the TravStats Companion app with your server through a QR code. Once paired, the server sends flight changes – gate, delay, cancellation, diversion – and departure reminders to the phone as push notifications, end-to-end encrypted through a relay an admin switches on; FlightAware AeroAPI with your own key can serve as the status source. The app stays in step with the server through a change log and never silently overwrites a newer version: if an entry changed in the meantime, it asks. Pairing, push and sync are built but, like the app itself, still being checked.

beta.title: Behind the beta switch: roadtrips, tours, rail, rental cars, bus, cruise tracks
beta.body: Roadtrips with stations at your stays, day tours with an elevation profile – a trip's map now draws its tours too –, rail as a domain of its own – with a station catalogue, a train-number lookup, the real line on the map, tickets and booking mails to import, rail achievements of its own and rail loyalty cards such as BahnBonus whose figures lead to the rides behind them –, rental cars as a domain of their own, coach rides as a domain of their own, recorded tracks on cruises – a GPS recording replaces the computed sea route of the legs it covers – and hotel enrichment from OpenStreetMap are built but still being checked. Which routing service computes roadtrips and tours is set by an admin under Administration → External services; you can store a key of your own under Settings → Services. With the switch on, countries you reached only by train or on a roadtrip count toward the country achievements too, and day tours join the trip suggestions. An admin turns it all on with the beta switch; each registry entry says when it comes out.

countries.title: Countries count by evidence, not by landing
countries.body: A country counts when something proves you were there: a completed stay, a recorded place, a port call, a night, a day driven through from your location history — no longer where a flight touched down. Every counted country names its evidence, how strictly is a setting (an instance default, overridable per account), and data that contradicts itself goes to the inbox instead of being corrected silently. The number moves for every account. The inbox is always in the menu now.

lodging.title: Hotels are a domain of their own
lodging.body: Stays are now kept like flights and cruises: with chain, room, board, per-category ratings, price, loyalty programme and the trip they belong to. They appear on the map as pins and count towards statistics and achievements — and switching the domain off removes it everywhere without touching your data.

documents.title: Bookings and documents are read for you, in any currency
documents.body: Booking.com mails are read by a deterministic template: measured against 95 real confirmations it finds the stay in 93 and the price in all 93 — across both layouts the sender uses. Anything it does not recognise takes the same AI path flights do. A document now announces itself: a photographed hotel bill is a document, a boarding pass is read by its barcode first, package-tour paperwork is recognised — and a marketing newsletter no longer becomes a flight. A price may be written in any currency. Conversion goes through the European Central Bank, and for the currencies it does not publish, through a free dataset you can switch off as the operator. Where no rate exists the amount stays in its own currency, is marked "no rate", counts towards no total — and the total tells you how many entries it is missing. You may enter a rate yourself; it is always shown as yours, never as an official one.

imports.title: In and out: spreadsheet and CSV
imports.body: The whole logbook exports to one spreadsheet and comes back — flights, cruises, stays. The CSV import shows what it will do first, asks about likely duplicates, and every import leaves a trace that can be taken back as a whole.

stats.title: Statistics and achievements have grown
stats.body: Records, the whole route network and the year in review come from the server, every statistics tab shows only the blocks you want, hotels have a chapter of their own, and every flight has a page to read it on. Plus 78 new achievements for places and hotels.

security.title: Two-factor and passkeys
security.body: You can protect your account with a second factor — TOTP, with single-use recovery codes — or with a passkey that replaces the password entirely. Both live in the new security section of the settings.

beta.title: The beta switch says what it turns on
beta.body: Unfinished areas sit behind a switch in the admin settings: places as a domain of their own with lists, checklists and the import of saved Google Maps lists, the passport, a colour per domain, the AI summary of a trip — and tours (a trip walked, driven, cycled, with a route editor), pairing with the TravStats Companion app and the Dawarich connection. Each entry says why it is still hidden and when it comes back. Off is the default; turn it on to test.

flightsTable.title: The flight table reads like a departures board
flightsTable.body: Every row now carries the airline as a brand tile, departure and arrival share one time column, country flags mark the route, and the actions are icons instead of text buttons. A dot on the row tells you where the data came from.

immich.title: Trip photos from your own Immich
immich.body: You can link Immich albums straight to a trip — either linked only, which keeps the images on your server and uses no storage here, or as a real import. The gallery groups by album, any picture can become the cover, and a re-sync picks up stragglers.

companions.title: Companions are real records now
companions.body: Travel companions are no longer free text on a single record. You create them once and reuse them everywhere — in flights, trips, cruises and special flights, through the same picker. Your existing entries are migrated automatically on startup.

flightForm.title: One flight form, scheduled and actual times
flightForm.body: Adding and editing finally use the same form. New: scheduled and actual times with the delay calculated for you, boarding group, trip assignment, cost and receipt — and airline and aircraft type come from the catalogue. A field you clear stays cleared instead of quietly keeping the old value.

status.title: Status follows from the dates
status.body: Whether something is planned, under way or done is now derived from its dates and refreshed hourly — for flights, cruises and trips alike. The manual status picker is gone as a result; the only state you still set yourself is "cancelled".

stats.title: Anonymous usage statistics
stats.body: TravStats can now optionally send anonymous usage data. It is off by default, and you can turn it back off at any time.

whatsNew.title: This dialog
whatsNew.body: After every update you will see a one-time summary of what changed.

colorModes.title: Map colors that listen to you
colorModes.body: Flight and cruise coloring are now proper modes: status, frequency, per journey, or a single custom color. The color picker finally works everywhere — and the legend always matches what the map actually shows.

airlines.title: Airlines by name
airlines.body: Instead of cryptic codes like "DLH" you now see "Lufthansa" — in the table, the list and the calendar. Flights that only carry an ICAO code now resolve correctly too.

map.title: The map, your way
map.body: New: flat 2D routes along the true great circle as an alternative to 3D arcs. Also: place names with special characters, consistent dot sizes for airports and ports, and direction arrows that sit right on long legs.

fixes.title: Reported bugs fixed
fixes.body: Profile picture and birthday now survive a reload, "Compare with" in statistics is remembered, and booking and ticket numbers can be entered right when adding a flight manually.

polish.title: A tidier interface
polish.body: The map menu remembers whether it was open, the year selector is readable again, buttons have better contrast — and unfinished features stay hidden by default until they are ready.
